rows.what the ink shows: Above the short cancellation, the initial t retains its upright and short left cross-stroke, followed by two close upright l ascenders. A low terminal sweep remains just beneath the right end of the cancellation; this surviving t–ll outline supports telle.

The initial accented e and two t uprights identify étant. The two following words are heavily overstruck: q-like descenders survive in the first, and an initial p descender, rounded o and detached dots survive in the second, but the intervening letter bodies are merged with cancellation lines, so quelconque positive remains uncertain. At the right, il has a separate dot and tall l loop; suffit retains the two tall f strokes, i dot and final crossed t; que retains its descending q and low connected ending.

The first word retains the tall b and lower bowl, a sequence of low rounded joins and a detached accent over its ending, supporting bornée; the comma is distinct. The following d ascender and terminal c tip, then the q loop and descender, support donc que. Farther right a tall p stem and a later descending loop remain, but the cancellation covers almost all low letter bodies between them and does not establish the complete par exemple sequence.

The capital E has a long left upright and clear top and middle horizontal strokes. Its continuation has a low hooked crossing compatible with x, but the thick sloping overstrike and lower looped remnants obscure the ending; no separate terminal dot is securely visible. The initial E can be resolved, while x. remains uncertain.
